recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-24651 unless Pharmacy and BR&R make a new current decision requiring MedicationKnowledge-specific BOSS/PAI modeling.
issue_request: Published Pharmacy issue FHIR-24651 asked to update MedicationKnowledge to include both Basis of Strength Substance (BOSS) and Precise Active Ingredient (PAI). Its final Not Persuasive with Modification resolution narrowed the applied change to making the MedicationKnowledge ingredient active indicator a CodeableConcept with an exemplar value set, while deferring remaining BOSS/PAI and Ingredient-resource role/entity questions to Pharmacy/BR&R follow-up work.
initial_application: Commit bb4b0e41393b1023027fc45c9e53d5d941c95ff3 explicitly included FHIR-24651 and changed MedicationKnowledge.ingredient.isActive from boolean to CodeableConcept with an example binding to v3 RoleClassIngredientEntity. Commit 6422f2f98a0fcf03140c15fe93bfd6c765fc6377 later moved the ingredient content under MedicationKnowledge.definitional.ingredient while preserving the CodeableConcept role/type representation and binding.
additional_context: MedicationKnowledge is active in the current build via source/fhir.ini. Current source defines MedicationKnowledge.definitional.ingredient.item as a CodeableReference to SubstanceDefinition and MedicationKnowledge.definitional.ingredient.type as a CodeableConcept bound at example strength to v3 RoleClassIngredientEntity. September 2020 Pharmacy WGM minutes match the Jira resolution and record that BOSS/PAI representation needed BR&R coordination rather than a direct MedicationKnowledge addition. Later BR&R issues FHIR-31599 and FHIR-31808 cover related Ingredient modeling and are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active authoritative source already contains the accepted CodeableConcept ingredient-role change, and adding direct BOSS/PAI fields or narrative to MedicationKnowledge now would exceed FHIR-24651's approved scope and risk conflicting with later Ingredient/BR&R modeling decisions.
